name: team_planning_status
description: Get the status of each planned change in a scenario of a Team Planning plan the caller is in, held against the Org Graph today (a UTC day, as known now). There is one status per subject and facet the scenario resolves, from its own changes and those it inherits from the scenarios it follows; scenario_id says which scenario made it (the plan_id is the baseline). 'done' when today reads the planned end state, 'pending' when today still reads what the plan's base held or what the step before plans, 'conflicting' when it reads none of these, 'unknown' when the plan's value was private and has since been removed, and 'plan_only' for a change the Org Graph never holds, such as a rule, a position, a capacity, a budget line, a hire the plan adds or a person's pay: it is never compared, so it is no Org Graph work still to do, and has no sources. On a plan scoped to some units, 'outside' marks a change about someone or some unit the plan no longer covers: the scope hides the organisation's data about them, so it is never compared and carries only scenario_id, change_id, subject_id and facet, plus the plan's own note, with no since, sources or name. Clear, undo or note it. Before the plan's base date nothing reads conflicting. A conflict an update to today carried forward still reads 'conflicting', with since the day of the update that first found it, while the scenario still resolves to the same change: a set, pin, clear or undo ends it. A change that reads done, unknown or plan_only keeps that status; otherwise since is null. Each status carries `sources`, who supplies what the change moves: the provider of a person fact (level, manager, leaving), or of the units an assignment, unit or succession touches, today and as planned ("espalia" for one Espalia supplies, or an HRIS such as "hibob"). A person's placements are one facet, so a placement list is done only when the whole list matches. The Org Graph can't say which position someone fills, only where they are, so a placement in a position is done once the person is in the position's unit at its allocation, with its role only when the plan names one. A unit retirement is done once the Org Graph has retired the unit. A unit succession is held against every succession the Org Graph recorded since the base that shares a planned predecessor, joined: done when they join to the planned sides, conflicting when they don't. A departure is done once the Org Graph has the person leave, and pending while they stay. A withdrawn departure carries staying: true; it is done while the person stays, and conflicting once the Org Graph has them leave. Subjects are named by id, and `names` maps each the Org Graph holds to a name; a forgotten person reads as "Former member", and a subject only the plan holds has none. A status whose change carries a note has it as note: { value }, or { removed: true } once erased. A note on a pay change reaches only a member with the see-pay right; anyone else gets no note on it. clearable is true on a status the caller may hand back to what the step before gives it with team_planning_clear_change: an editor's, on a change the scenario makes itself, never on the baseline, and never on a pay change without the see-pay right. A change about someone or something a scoped plan no longer covers is clearable like any other, so it can be removed. Such a status, read as outside, also carries undoable: true when team_planning_undo_change on its change_id would take it out and bring no earlier change back, since that would name what the plan no longer covers. An archived plan is not checked: it returns checked: false, archived_on and a note, with nothing listed, so an empty list never reads as nothing wrong. Restoring the plan checks it again; otherwise checked is true. Refused, as an unknown plan, unless the caller is a member.

scenario_id.description: The scenario, or the plan's id for the baseline.
